shortDescription: A dense tropical coastal capital where an extended household moves through Ghanaian public schooling, trotros, shared taxis, open markets, community programs and multilingual everyday life.
longDescription: The World is rooted in Accra, Ghana, where two caregivers, a child and two cousins share a compact home on a busy residential-commercial street. English structures formal schooling and many civic settings while Twi is common in household, market, media and everyday conversation within a much more multilingual city. Trotros, shared taxis, markets, local media, public-health services and extended-family ties create a wide everyday social field. Across 2004–2026, mobile phones, digital services and urban growth become increasingly visible while heat, seasonal rain, Harmattan conditions, street commerce and shared transport remain persistent features.

visualProfile.overallCharacter: Energetic ordinary Accra street life: dense commerce, shared transport, extended households and community institutions, shown without generic 'Africa' visual shorthand.
visualProfile.geographyAndClimate: Warm tropical coastal capital with strong sun, humidity, seasonal heavy rains and periodic Harmattan haze/dust; the coast is part of metropolitan geography rather than a resort backdrop.
visualProfile.builtEnvironment: Compact family homes, painted concrete/masonry buildings, small businesses, Ghanaian public-school facilities, open-market structures, community-program spaces and dense mixed commercial streets.
visualProfile.streetsAndPublicRealm: Busy pedestrian edges, roadside vendors, trotro/shared-taxi junctions, market lanes, school grounds, neighborhood meeting spaces and traffic congestion; shade and shelter matter in both sun and rain.
visualProfile.interiors: Compact shared household rooms, public-school classrooms/science spaces/reading rooms, community multipurpose rooms, market stalls, repair counters and ordinary small-business interiors.
visualProfile.materialsAndTextures: Painted concrete and masonry, metal roofs or awnings where appropriate, fabric canopies, wood/metal stalls, road dust or wet pavement depending on season, plastic crates, tools, electronics, school notices and everyday goods.
visualProfile.lightAndAtmosphere: Intense tropical daylight, humid brightness, deep shade under awnings, rain-darkened streets, Harmattan-softened skies at some times of year and warm evening commercial lighting.
visualProfile.vegetationAndLandscape: Tropical street trees and planted compounds can appear within a primarily dense urban environment; coast and vegetation should support, not replace, everyday city life.
visualProfile.mobilityAndVehicles: Walking, trotros and shared taxis dominate routine movement; buses, commercial vans, motorcycles and ordinary cars may appear, but private-car ownership should not define the household.
visualProfile.signageAndLanguage: English should dominate formal school/civic signs. Twi can appear naturally in market, media or informal commercial contexts, while other Ghanaian languages may be present incidentally; avoid making the streets visually monolingual or inventing political slogans.
visualProfile.clothingAndEverydayObjects: Contemporary everyday Ghanaian urban clothing across ages; school bags/materials, phones, market totes, radios, fabric, repair tools, electronics, public-health materials and transport fare/payment objects. Traditional or formal clothing may appear contextually but is not default daily costume.
visualProfile.technologyAndInfrastructure: The chronology moves from feature phones and cash-heavy commerce toward smartphones, mobile data, mobile money and more digital services; schools, markets, trotros, utilities and neighborhood commerce remain visible throughout.
visualProfile.publicInstitutions: Ghanaian public school, market networks, trotro/shared-taxi transport, neighborhood community programs, public-health services and local media should feel embedded in ordinary metropolitan life.

temporalLayers.2004_2010: Feature phones, less pervasive mobile data, more cash-only transactions and older trotro/vehicle cues; public school, market and shared-transport life remain strongly recognizable.
temporalLayers.2011_2018: Smartphones, social media and mobile money become increasingly visible; urban growth and digital commerce expand while neighborhood markets and trotros remain central.
temporalLayers.2019_2026: Smartphone-centered services, mobile payments, newer commercial signage and expanding digital infrastructure can appear alongside persistent shared transport, open markets and community institutions.
temporalLayers.continuities: English/Twi everyday context, heat and seasonal weather, trotro mobility, street commerce, extended-family geography, schools and markets remain stable visual anchors.

avoid: national monuments or flags used as the primary location shorthand
